subject: Psi-8 p95 surge: request to hold traffic fraction and enable fallback
messages:
From: Daniel Chu <daniel@brightshift.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightShift Platform Team <ops@brightshift.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden p95 spike on Psi-8 since 06:00 UTC — can we hold traffic?

Hi Evelyn,

We're seeing a sharp p95 tail increase for the psi-8 model that started around 06:00 UTC this morning. Baselines were ~240ms; current p95 is ~980ms for inference requests with average sequence length 280 tokens. Error rates are low but latency is causing timeouts in our orchestration layer and user-facing retries.

We've attached a short report and traces. Quick notes from our side:
- The spike appears correlated with requests that hit the new fp16-quant variant (psi-8-fp16) that rolled at 60% traffic overnight.
- Memory/CPU on our side is healthy; KV cache hit rate dropped marginally when the variant was selected.
- Rolling back the variant on our side reduces tail to ~320ms in preliminary tests.

Can Redwood hold traffic to psi-8-fp16 (reduce to 0% or 10%) and enable the psi-7-stable fallback while we investigate? We need an authorization path or quick rollback window — otherwise we will start rerouting on our side which will affect the joint rollout.

Thanks,
Daniel Chu
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightShift

Attachments: latency_report_psi8-20290314.pdf, service-trace-psi8-20290314.log

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p95 spike on Psi-8 since 06:00 UTC — can we hold traffic?

Marcus/Ben/Priya — looping you in. BrightShift reports p95 ~980ms after the psi-8-fp16 roll to 60% traffic. They saw fallback to psi-7-stable reduce tail to ~320ms.

Can we do an immediate protective action: reduce traffic fraction to psi-8-fp16 to 10% and open the automatic fallback to psi-7-stable for requests >700ms? If we agree, request that Legal/Commercial (Ben) confirm whether the temporary reroute is within our SLA carveout for canary instability — I'll include the external note to keep BrightShift aligned.

If we can't get hold approval within 30 minutes, I propose an emergency rollback of the fp16 variant back to the previous binary on the rollout channel. Marcus: what is the expected rollback window and risk?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p95 spike on Psi-8 since 06:00 UTC — can we hold traffic?

Evelyn — we can do either protective traffic hold or rollback. Quick bullets: 
- Traffic hold to 10% for psi-8-fp16: ~2 minutes to change routing policy, zero deploy risk. Fallback to psi-7-stable for requests >700ms: can enable via routing rule, but will increase overall compute usage by ~7-12% until stabilized.
- Full rollback of psi-8-fp16 to previous build: estimated 12–15 minute window to drain existing sessions and redeploy the previous image across the pool. Rollback risk low but will temporarily reduce capacity if no burst headroom.

Recommendation: do an immediate traffic hold to 10% AND enable psi-7-stable fallback >700ms. If p95 remains >450ms after 45 minutes, authorize rollback. I'll standby to execute both actions.

—Marcus
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p95 spike on Psi-8 since 06:00 UTC — can we hold traffic?

Eve — Approved. It's within our incident SLA carveout for rollout instability; authorize traffic hold to 10% and fallback to psi-7-stable for >700ms. Please keep BrightShift updated and flag any billing/credits implications — we will review post-mortem.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Chu <daniel@brightshift.ai>, BrightShift Platform Team <ops@brightshift.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p95 spike on Psi-8 since 06:00 UTC — can we hold traffic?

Hi Daniel — thanks for the quick flag and the diagnostic package.

Actions taken (per Ben/Marcus approval):
- We reduced psi-8-fp16 routing fraction to 10% at 09:05 PDT.
- Enabled automatic fallback to psi-7-stable for requests that exceed 700ms.
- We've also spun up an extra dedicated slot in us-west for the fallback pool to limit capacity pressure.

Observed impact: p95 across your workload dropped to ~340ms within 20 minutes of the routing hold. CPU margins increased slightly due to fallbacks but stayed within expected burst headroom. 

Next steps:
- Marcus/Serving team to run a focused perf/kv-cache investigation on the fp16 path (we suspect a regression in kernel selection with sequence-length variance).
- BrightShift to share a sampling of calls (we have the traces) and any workload shape changes that coincide with the rollout.
- If we still see p95 >450ms for more than 45 minutes, we'll proceed with a rollback of the fp16 variant per Marcus' plan.

We will keep you posted on status and a post-mortem/credit discussion once we have root cause.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
